problems.code:
def count_nums(arr)
  arr.count do |num|
    digits = num.to_s.chars
    if digits.first == '-'
      # For negative numbers, make the first digit negative
      digits[1..-1] = digits[1..-1].map(&:to_i)
      digits[0] = -digits[0].to_i
    else
      digits = digits.map(&:to_i)
    end
    
    sum = digits.sum
    sum > 0
  end
end

problems.name: HumanEval_111_histogram

def histogram(test)
  return {} if test.empty?
  
  letters = test.split(' ')
  counts = Hash.new(0)
  
  letters.each { |letter| counts[letter] += 1 }
  
  max_count = counts.values.max
  result = {}
  
  counts.each do |letter, count|
    if count == max_count
      result[letter] = count
    end
  end
  
  result
end

def get_row(lst, x)
  result = []
  
  lst.each_with_index do |row, row_idx|
    row.each_with_index do |value, col_idx|
      if value == x
        result << [row_idx, col_idx]

def how_many_times(string, substring)
  return 0 if string.empty? || substring.empty?
  
  count = 0
  start = 0
  
  while start <= string.length - substring.length
    pos = string.index(substring, start)
    break unless pos
    
    count += 1
    start = pos + 1
  end
  
  count
end

  vowels = 'aeiou'
  result = ''
  
  message.each_char do |char|
    if char.match?(/[a-z]/i)
      # Swap case
      swapped_case = char.swapcase
      
      # Replace vowels with letter 2 places ahead
      if vowels.include?(swapped_case.downcase)
        vowel_index = vowels.index(swapped_case.downcase)
        replacement_vowel = vowels[(vowel_index + 2) % vowels.length]
        
        # Preserve original case
        if swapped_case == swapped_case.upcase
          result += replacement_vowel.upcase
        else
          result += replacement_vowel
        end
      else
        result += swapped_case
      end
    else
      result += char
    end
  end
  
  result
end

  return false if txt.empty?

def minPath(grid, k)
  n = grid.length
  directions = [[0, 1], [1, 0], [0, -1], [-1, 0]]
  
  # Find all possible starting positions and their values
  start_positions = []
  (0...n).each do |i|
    (0...n).each do |j|
      start_positions << [grid[i][j], i, j]
    end
  end
  
  # Sort by value to try smaller values first
  start_positions.sort!
  
  min_path = nil
  
  # Try each starting position
  start_positions.each do |val, start_i, start_j|
    # BFS to find all paths of length k from this starting point
    queue = [[start_i, start_j, [val]]]
    
    while !queue.empty?
      i, j, path = queue.shift
      
      if path.length == k
        # Check if this is the minimum lexicographically
        if min_path.nil? || path < min_path
          min_path = path.dup
        end
        next
      end
      
      # Generate neighbors
      directions.each do |di, dj|
        ni, nj = i + di, j + dj
        
        # Check bounds
        if ni >= 0 && ni < n && nj >= 0 && nj < n
          new_path = path.dup
          new_path << grid[ni][nj]
          
          # Early termination: if current path is already larger than min_path,
          # we don't need to explore further
          if min_path && new_path > min_path[0, new_path.length]
            next
          end
          
          queue << [ni, nj, new_path]
        end
      end
    end
    
    # If we found a solution and it's minimal, break early
    break if min_path && min_path.length == k
  end
  
  min_path || []
end

def intersection(interval1, interval2)
  # Find the intersection of two intervals
  start = [interval1[0], interval2[0]].max
  end_val = [interval1[1], interval2[1]].min
  
  # If there's no intersection
  if start > end_val
    return "NO"
  end
  
  # Calculate the length of intersection (inclusive)
  length = end_val - start + 1
  
  # Check if the length is a prime number
  if is_prime(length)
    return "YES"
  else
    return "NO"
  end
end

def is_prime(n)
  # Handle edge cases
  if n < 2
    return false
  end
  
  if n == 2
    return true
  end
  
  if n % 2 == 0
    return false
  end
  
  # Check odd divisors up to sqrt(n)
  i = 3
  while i * i <= n
    if n % i == 0
      return false
    end
    i += 2
  end
  
  return true
end

def triples_sum_to_zero(l)
  return false if l.length < 3
  
  # Sort the array to enable two-pointer technique
  sorted = l.sort
  
  # Iterate through each element as the first element of potential triple
  (0...sorted.length - 2).each do |i|
    # Use two pointers to find pairs that sum to negative of current element
    left = i + 1
    right = sorted.length - 1
    
    while left < right
      sum = sorted[i] + sorted[left] + sorted[right]
      
      if sum == 0
        return true
      elsif sum < 0
        left += 1
      else
        right -= 1
      end
    end
  end
  
  false
end

  # Convert inputs to comparable numeric values

      # Try to parse as float first, then integer

    s.reverse

      return false if num % i == 0
    end

  end
